name: truncnorm
resume: All six exports of truncnorm 1.0-9 are checked. The density and cdf use extraDistr's normal functions, which are math.erf. The mean uses SciPy's log cdf so a far tail does not underflow. Draws use extraDistr's generators on boot's Mersenne-Twister. There is no crate.

functions.name: dtruncnorm
functions.done: Density on an interval. A point outside it is 0. A zero-length argument is NULL.

check.case: Density at -2, 0, and 2 on (-1, 1). Outside the interval the density is 0.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(truncnorm))
one <- function() {
  paste(sprintf("%.17g", dtruncnorm(c(-2, 0, 2), -1, 1)), collapse = ",")
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
shown <- enc2utf8(paste(as.character(value), collapse = "|"))
shown <- gsub("\n", " / ", shown, fixed = TRUE)
cat("VALUE ", shown, "\n", sep = "")
cat(sprintf("MS %.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
from truncnorm import dtruncnorm

def one():
    return ",".join(f"{v:.17g}" for v in dtruncnorm([-2, 0, 2], -1, 1))

import statistics
import time
value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print("VALUE " + str(value).replace("\n", " / "))
print(f"MS {statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: qtruncnorm
functions.done: Quantile by Brent's zeroin. An infinite bound is stepped in until the bracket is finite.

check.case: Quantiles on a finite interval, a right-truncated normal, and a left-truncated normal.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(truncnorm))
one <- function() {
  paste(sprintf("%.17g", qtruncnorm(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.9), c(-1, -Inf, -1), c(2, 1, Inf))), collapse = ",")
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {

functions.name: rtruncnorm
functions.done: Accept-reject draws on boot's Mersenne-Twister, so set.seed(1) matches R.

check.case: Five draws on (-1, 1) after set.seed(1). They use boot's Mersenne-Twister.

functions.name: etruncnorm
functions.done: Mean. A far interval is the midpoint. The log cdf is SciPy's, because log(erf) underflows.

check.case: Means of a central interval, a far interval, a left tail, and a long left tail.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(truncnorm))
one <- function() {
  paste(sprintf("%.17g", c(etruncnorm(-1, 1), etruncnorm(8, 9), etruncnorm(1, Inf), etruncnorm(-20, 0))), collapse = ",")
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0

proof.python:
